overview: Two types of T cells with different jobs — one coordinates the immune response, the other directly kills infected cells.
genZNote: Helper T cells: the immune system's project managers. Cytotoxic T cells: the ones who actually pull the trigger.

aspects.label: Main Role
aspects.valueA: Coordinates and activates other immune cells (B cells, macrophages, cytotoxic T cells) by releasing cytokines.
aspects.valueB: Directly kills infected, cancerous, or foreign cells.

aspects.label: MHC Restriction
aspects.valueA: Recognises antigen presented on MHC class II.
aspects.valueB: Recognises antigen presented on MHC class I.

aspects.label: Relevance to HIV
aspects.valueA: The primary target of HIV, which is why HIV infection is so devastating to immunity.
aspects.valueB: Not the primary target of HIV, though their function is eventually compromised as CD4+ helper T cells decline.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: HIV specifically targets CD4+ helper T cells, which is why a falling CD4 count is used to track AIDS progression.
overlay.memoryTrick: Helper T = CD4, coordinates. Cytotoxic T = CD8, kills directly.
overlay.commonMisconception: Cytotoxic T cells are not the same as natural killer (NK) cells — cytotoxic T cells are antigen-specific and part of adaptive immunity, while NK cells act non-specifically as part of innate immunity.
